purpose: Expand the evergreen topic reserve with distinct money-management habits and investor decision behaviours, while keeping the editorial focus on mindset rather than financial headlines.
comparison_basis: Screened against the 45 existing topic blueprints and the previous inspiration pools. Similar angles were rejected or narrowed; the accepted list below focuses on distinct behaviours or decision errors.

candidates.title: Your money needs a regular check-in, not an annual resolution
candidates.distinct_angle: A recurring review habit, distinct from making a one-time budget.

candidates.title: Decide what enough means before comparison moves the goalposts
candidates.distinct_angle: Defines personal sufficiency and values, rather than comparing visible lifestyles.

candidates.title: Annual expenses are not surprises if you plan for them
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on predictable but non-monthly costs, distinct from unexpected emergencies.

candidates.title: Keeping money records creates clarity, not a reason for guilt
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on financial record-keeping as information, not shame or avoidance.

candidates.title: Agree on money expectations before making shared commitments
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on clear roles and expectations before shared obligations.

candidates.title: A simple money routine works when motivation disappears
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on routine design rather than general discipline slogans.

candidates.title: Let your values guide spending more than the mood of the moment
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on values-based choices when emotions influence optional spending.

candidates.title: Changing your money plan is not the same as giving up
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on flexible plan revision, distinct from simply starting small.

candidates.title: One difficult month does not define your financial future
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on preventing one setback from becoming an identity or permanent conclusion.

candidates.title: Pause before making important money decisions in a strong emotion
candidates.distinct_angle: A cooling-off decision habit for high-emotion commitments, not only impulse purchases.

candidates.title: Make your financial progress visible instead of demanding perfection
candidates.distinct_angle: Uses visible progress and realistic baselines rather than perfect streaks.

candidates.title: A familiar investment is not automatically a safe investment
candidates.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Investor.gov
candidates.distinct_angle: Explains familiarity bias; recognition is not risk analysis.

candidates.title: Past investment performance is a record, not a promise
candidates.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Investor.gov
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on extrapolating past performance, not generic get-rich-quick promises.

candidates.title: More investment activity does not automatically mean better decisions
candidates.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Investor.gov
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on active-trading behaviour and confusing activity with decision quality.

candidates.title: Panic is not an investment strategy
candidates.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Investor.gov
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on crowd panic and emotional reactions to market movements.

candidates.title: A popular investment still deserves independent research
candidates.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Investor.gov
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on momentum and social proof, with an explicit research action.

candidates.title: Owning many investments does not automatically mean you are diversified
candidates.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Investor.gov
candidates.distinct_angle: Clarifies naïve diversification without recommending a specific portfolio.

candidates.title: Do not overlook fees while focusing on investment performance
candidates.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Investor.gov
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on neglecting fees when judging performance.

candidates.title: Write down your reasons before changing an investment plan
candidates.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Investor.gov
candidates.distinct_angle: A decision-journal habit to reduce reactive changes; not a recommendation to hold or sell.

candidates.title: Check the source before sharing a money claim with others
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on information verification and responsible sharing, not scam detection alone.

candidates.title: Asking for clarity is a strength, not a sign of weakness
candidates.distinct_angle: Focuses on confidence to ask plain-language questions before agreeing to financial terms.

evidence_limitations: Source-page reachability and keyword matching do not establish that every sentence in a future script is supported.
The SEC Investor Bulletin describes U.S. investor behaviour research; use it for general behavioural education, not as a statement of Ugandan regulation.
Investment topics must remain educational and must not become personalized investment recommendations.
All topics remain candidates until claim-level evidence, geography and script quality are reviewed.
next_step: Run the repository research refresh to create candidate records; manually review claims before production.
